text: A fluorescence measurement depends on both excitation and collection. Supplied wavelength ranges can establish whether an optical path overlaps a signal band. Overlap alone does not establish adequate sensitivity. A saturated detector loses quantitative information even when the channel wavelengths are compatible.

Quantification is conditional on the calibration regime, measurement geometry and sample context. A numerical response outside a validated range does not acquire validity merely because a fitted equation returns a number. Unreported critical conditions should be distinguished from conditions explicitly shown to be incompatible.

An assay readout and the biological quantity of interest are different objects. A supporting experiment should distinguish a change in the detection chemistry from a change in the measured process. Conclusions should be scoped to the system studied; activity in a purified assay does not by itself measure an intracellular effect.
